lesson.title: Plants Resemble Their Parent Plants Too
lesson.subject: science

contentBlocks.text: Yesterday you saw young animals resemble their parents. Today: plants show this same pattern!

A seed from an apple tree grows into a new apple tree, not a different kind of plant. A sunflower seed grows into a sunflower, with the same kind of leaves, flower, and general shape as the parent plant. This is the same resemblance pattern you saw in animals yesterday, just in plants. Name a plant you know, and describe what its seed grows into.
You now see this pattern in both animals and plants — offspring resemble their parents! Tomorrow we'll look at how offspring can still be a little different from their parents too.

objectives: Describe that a plant's seed grows into the same kind of plant as its parent
Connect this pattern to yesterday's animal-resemblance content
materialsNeeded: A real seed or plant, if available
teacherGuide.facilitationScript:
1. Review yesterday's animal-resemblance content.
2. Introduce the apple-seed/apple-tree example.
3. Discuss a plant the child knows and what its seed grows into.
4. Complete the worksheet.
5. Close by explicitly connecting today's plant pattern to yesterday's animal pattern.
differentiationTips: Struggling: use a very familiar example (like a seed the child has planted or seen) rather than an abstract one
Ready for more: ask the child to explain why an apple seed never grows into an orange tree
If a real seed or plant is available, use it — concrete, physical examples work best at this age
teacherGuide.answerKey: This is a discussion and drawing activity — check that the child can explain a seed grows into the same kind of plant as its parent.
teacherGuide.standardsRationale: Directly addresses NGSS Grade 1 standard 1-LS3-1, extending yesterday's animal-resemblance pattern to plants, showing the same biological pattern across both kingdoms.
